justification.text: `(∑_{k<N} f(n_k x)) / N` is the problem's Cesàro average of the first N terms, because the claim is `Tendsto … atTop`, a statement about N → ∞, and N ≥ 1 for every index but the first; the junk value at N = 0 (an empty sum over 0) is one term and cannot affect a limit.

`1 / (log log log k)^C` is the problem's O(1/(log log log k)^C) bound, because the hypothesis is `=O[atTop]`, which constrains only large k, and for every k ≥ 16 we have log k > e, so log log k > 1 and log log log k > 0, making the denominator positive; the finitely many smaller k are outside the eventual range.

`log (log (log k))` is the problem's iterated logarithm, because inside the `=O[atTop]` hypothesis only large k matter and for k ≥ 16 all three logarithms have positive argument (log k > e > 1, log log k > 1 > 0), so no junk value occurs in the range the claim depends on.

`log (log k)` is the problem's log log k, because it occurs only inside the `=O[atTop]` bound and for every k ≥ 3 we have log k > 1 > 0, so its argument is positive on the eventual range; the junk values at k ≤ 2 cannot affect an eventual bound.
